overview: Chery Automobile is a Wuhu, Anhui-headquartered Chinese passenger vehicle manufacturer that designs, develops, manufactures and sells ICE vehicles and new energy vehicles (NEVs) under five brands: CHERY (including OMODA, JAECOO and LEPAS for overseas markets), JETOUR, EXEED, iCAR and LUXEED. The company listed on the Main Board of the Hong Kong Stock Exchange in September 2025 (stock code 9973) in the largest global automotive IPO of 2025, raising roughly US$1.2 billion. Chery is China's largest passenger-vehicle exporter (for 23 consecutive years) and in 2025 became the first Chinese automaker to surpass 5 million cumulative vehicle exports, with 12 production bases worldwide including 3 overseas (as of mid-2026).

business_model.summary: Chery manufactures and sells passenger vehicles (the large majority of revenue) plus automotive parts/components and other supporting services (including KD kit assembly and technology licensing). Revenue is reported as RMB300.3bn for FY2025 (+11.3% YoY) and RMB143.3bn for H1 2026 (+1.2% YoY). The mix is shifting rapidly from ICE to NEV: NEVs were 21.9% of 2024 revenue, rising to 32.6% in FY2025 and 41.4% in H1 2026, while ICE vehicles fell from 69.6% to 58.1% to 48.5% of revenue over the same stretch. Gross margin has improved materially (13.0% H1 2025 to 16.1% H1 2026) as overseas sales, which carry higher margins than domestic sales, have grown to nearly 100bn RMB in H1 2026 (+51% YoY) and now represent roughly 40%+ of group revenue. Revenue is overwhelmingly transactional (vehicle unit sales) rather than recurring/subscription-based, though parts/components and technology-licensing revenue provide some ancillary, higher-margin streams.

revenue_streams.name: Passenger vehicles - ICE
revenue_streams.trend: declining as % of mix (was 65.3% in H1 2025)

revenue_streams.name: Automotive parts and components
revenue_streams.trend: growing, driven by overseas vehicle sales

business_model.customer_type: B2C (retail car buyers via dealer networks domestically and overseas) with some B2B/government fleet and technology-licensing revenue; distinct brand positioning for mass-market (CHERY/JETOUR), premium (EXEED), Gen-Z EV (iCAR) and smart/tech-forward (LUXEED) segments
business_model.geographic_mix: Exports were 1.294 million vehicles in FY2025 (+33.2% YoY, ~49% of 2.631 million total unit sales); overseas revenue reached ~RMB99bn in H1 2026 (+51% YoY), approaching 70% of total revenue on an annualized run-rate basis. Key export markets include Russia, Turkey, and an expanding footprint across 16 European countries (sales +200% YoY in FY2025, Omoda/Jaecoo accounting for ~41.5% of global brand sales from Europe in March 2026), plus South America, Africa and the Middle East. Products sold in 100+ countries.

main_competitors: Xpeng, NIO and other NEV-native entrants
Volkswagen, Toyota and other legacy global OEMs in overseas/ICE segments
competitive_position.market_position: China's second-largest passenger-vehicle seller by volume historically (behind BYD) and the largest Chinese vehicle exporter for 23 straight years; in China's domestic NEV retail market Chery ranks outside the top 5 (~7th, ~4.6% share as of August 2026) well behind BYD (~23%) and Geely (~11%), but Chery is a top-2 player in NEV exports (2nd behind BYD, ~15% share in July 2026) and 1st in overall passenger-vehicle exports (~21.7% share). Omoda/Jaecoo surpassed 1 million cumulative global sales by April 2026 and lead UK/European sales charts for Chinese brands in several months of 2026.

moat_factors.description: 23 consecutive years as China's top vehicle exporter, 12 production bases (3 overseas as of H1 2026) including a Spanish JV, and distribution in 100+ countries give Chery a first-mover logistics, dealer-network and regulatory-compliance advantage that is difficult and slow for domestic-focused rivals to replicate.

Five distinct brands (CHERY, JETOUR, EXEED, iCAR, LUXEED) plus overseas sub-brands (OMODA, JAECOO, LEPAS) allow segmentation across mass-market, family/outdoor, premium, Gen-Z EV and tech-forward buyers, broadening addressable demand versus single-brand peers.

Proprietary ACTECO engine series and the Kunpeng hybrid-dedicated engines (CDM-O 2.0TD, Kunpeng Tianqing with >48% thermal efficiency) have won 'China Heart Top Ten Engines' 12 times, supporting a 'China New Fuel' hybrid/ICE-upgrade strategy that differentiates Chery from pure-BEV-focused rivals, though this is a narrowing advantage as NEV adoption accelerates.

Industry-leading J.D. Power scores (ranked #1 among domestic brands across IQS, SSI, CSI, APEAL and VDS in 2025) and 60 models with five-star global safety ratings support a 'Chery of Quality' positioning that aids premiumization and export credibility.

2.631 million units sold in FY2025 provides purchasing and manufacturing scale, though Chery's domestic NEV market share and margins still trail BYD's, limiting cost-leadership relative to the segment leader.

weaknesses: Lags BYD, Geely and others in China's fast-growing domestic NEV market (~4.6% retail share vs. BYD's ~23%), remaining more ICE-weighted domestically than top NEV peers

Lower overall gross margin (13.8% FY2025, 16.1% H1 2026) than many global peers, with NEV gross margins still well below ICE margins (8.8% vs. 15.0% in FY2025), implying continued margin dilution as the NEV mix rises further

Heavy reliance on export growth (overseas sales +51% YoY in H1 2026) to offset a roughly flat domestic/total revenue backdrop, creating concentration risk in a handful of markets (Russia, Turkey, Europe) subject to tariff and geopolitical shocks

No current access to the US market (100%+ tariffs on Chinese EVs, data-security restrictions), ceding the world's second-largest auto market to peers already exploring workarounds (Mexico/Canada manufacturing, US partnerships)
Pre-IPO investor lock-up expiry (approaching as of September 2026, reportedly an ~US$8bn overhang) creates a near-term share-supply risk

growth_drivers: Continued overseas expansion: exports grew 33.2% in FY2025 to 1.294 million units and overseas revenue grew 51% YoY in H1 2026 to ~RMB99bn, with deepening penetration into regulated markets (16 European countries, Spain JV) and new markets (South America, Africa, Middle East)

NEV mix shift: NEV revenue share rose from 21.9% (2024) to 41.4% (H1 2026), with NEV gross margin improving sharply (0.4% in 2024 to 8.8% in FY2025) as scale and technology mature, narrowing the margin gap with ICE
Omoda/Jaecoo brand momentum in Europe/UK, targeting 1 million annual sales by 2027, with Jaecoo 7 among the UK's best-selling cars and hybrid (SHS) technology driving over 10,000 units/month

Technology investment in solid-state batteries, large AI models, and advanced smart/autonomous driving ('Falcon Advanced Intelligent Driving', 'Lingxi Intelligent Cabin' AI cockpit) to support premiumization and intelligent-vehicle differentiation

Five strategic priorities for 2026: brand elevation, global market expansion, technology innovation, moving up the industrial-ecosystem value chain, and management excellence, aimed at balancing speed, scale, quality and profitability
Diversification into adjacent robotics/embodied-AI products (humanoid robot 'Mornine', robot dog 'Argos') as an early-stage ecosystem extension beyond core automotive
Potential future US market entry via partnership with an American automaker or manufacturing in Mexico/Canada, which, if policy shifts allow, would open a large incremental addressable market

business.description: China's NEV and ICE markets remain hyper-competitive with aggressive price discounting led by BYD and others; Chery's domestic gross margins for passenger vehicles remain in the 12-16% range and NEV margins, while improving, are still well below ICE margins.

Managing five brands (CHERY, JETOUR, EXEED, iCAR, LUXEED) plus overseas sub-brands requires continuous differentiation and marketing spend (selling/distribution expense +32.6% YoY in FY2025); failure to maintain distinct positioning could dilute brand equity or cannibalize models.

Reliance on a diversified supplier network for steel, battery cells, electronic components and other inputs exposes Chery to price volatility and potential supply disruptions, as explicitly flagged in interim filings.

business.risk: Execution risk on new model launches
business.description: Growth depends on continued successful launches (Fulwin A9L, ZongHeng G700, LUXEED R7, iCAR V23/V27, JAECOO5, LUXEED V9); delays in development, production or delivery could undermine competitiveness.

financial.description: Gearing ratio (total liabilities/total assets) was 81.7% as of 30 June 2026, up from 80.4% at FY2025-end, reflecting a capital structure reliant on trade payables (RMB145.7bn as of H1 2026, +32.2% in six months) more than bank debt (bank loans and borrowings fell to RMB10.0bn from RMB15.9bn).

Net current assets fell 40.6% in H1 2026 (to RMB5.7bn) as inventories (+30.2% to RMB47.8bn) and trade receivables (+19.5% to RMB40.5bn) grew faster than cash, partly funding overseas expansion; a slowdown in export sell-through could strand inventory.

Cash holdings are multi-currency (RMB, EUR, USD, and formerly HKD) reflecting large European and other overseas operations; the Group uses FX forward contracts to hedge transactional exposure, but earnings remain sensitive to RMB/EUR/USD moves given >50% of revenue now generated overseas.

Profit attributable to owners fell in H1 2026 (reported RMB8.57bn vs. RMB9.9bn/profit-for-period figures in the prior-year period per press reports, roughly -12% YoY) even as revenue and gross margin improved, reflecting higher R&D (+28.3%), administrative expense growth and lower other income/FX gains (-27.1%).

regulatory.description: EU tariffs on Chinese EVs reached 35.3% (on top of the standard 10% duty) as of 2026, directly affecting Chery's largest growth export region; the company delayed Spanish EV production plans in response to provisional tariffs, though a JV in Spain is proceeding and some peers (e.g., Cupra/VW) have secured tariff exemptions via minimum-price/quota deals that Chinese automakers are now seeking to replicate.

100%+ US tariffs on Chinese EVs plus connected-car data-security restrictions keep Chery out of the world's second-largest auto market; as of October 2026 Chery has no confirmed US entry timeline, though it has expressed openness to partnerships with US automakers and is examining Mexico/Canada as alternative footholds.

New Chinese government requirements for special export permits (aimed at curbing price wars in overseas markets) could constrain Chery's export volumes or pricing flexibility, though they may also support healthier industry-wide margins over time.

As a newly listed (Sept 2025) HKEX issuer, Chery is subject to evolving compliance, continuous disclosure and corporate governance obligations under HK Listing Rules, with a relatively short track record as a public company.

macro.description: NEV demand in China is explicitly flagged by management as 'cyclical, policy-driven, and volatile,' tied to subsidy regimes and trade-in incentive programs that can shift abruptly.

Rising US-China and EU-China trade friction, tariff escalation risk, and broader geopolitical uncertainty in key export markets (including Russia-related sanctions exposure) could disrupt Chery's export-led growth model.
Exposure to steel, battery cell (lithium/other raw materials), and other component price volatility affects cost of sales, which represented ~86% of revenue in H1 2026.

execution.description: Reports (September 2026) flag an approaching pre-IPO investor lock-up expiry representing a potentially large (reportedly ~US$8bn) share overhang that could pressure the stock if cornerstone/pre-IPO holders (Hillhouse, Greenwoods, Dajia Life, Gotion, state-owned entities, etc.) begin selling.

execution.risk: First year as a public company
execution.description: Listed only since September 2025, Chery has limited public-market financial reporting history and investor-relations track record, adding uncertainty to forecasting and governance assessment relative to longer-tenured peers.

macro_factors.industry_outlook: China remains the world's largest auto producer/seller for the 17th consecutive year, with Chinese brands holding ~70% of domestic passenger-vehicle share and NEV penetration continuing to rise. China is also the world's largest auto exporter, with the industry shifting from pure product export to a full 'ecosystem globalization' model (local R&D, manufacturing, supply chain, branding, service). Global industry competition in 2026 centers on electrification, intelligent/autonomous technology, low-carbon solutions, AI and premiumization, with rapid market restructuring.
macro_factors.cyclicality: Moderate-to-high. Vehicle demand is cyclical and sensitive to consumer discretionary spending, government subsidy/incentive cycles (especially for NEVs in China), and trade-policy shocks in export markets; Chery's own filings explicitly characterize NEV demand as cyclical and policy-driven.
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: Moderate. The Group carries floating-rate bank borrowings (interest rate risk acknowledged in filings) and consumer auto financing/affordability is sensitive to broader interest-rate conditions in key markets, though Chery's own debt levels are relatively modest and declining (bank loans fell from RMB23.2bn in FY2024 to RMB10.0bn by H1 2026).
key_input_costs: Battery cells and other EV components

recent_developments.event: Chery executive told Reuters the company remains 'very open' to partnering with US automakers as Chinese carmakers stay effectively locked out of the US market (100%+ EV tariffs, data-security restrictions); no confirmed US entry timeline, with Chery instead focused on Europe, Latin America, the Middle East and Southeast Asia, and reportedly planning a Canada brand launch.
Market commentary (Smartkarma/Aequitas) flagged Chery's approaching pre-IPO investor lock-up expiry, representing a potentially large (~US$8bn) share-supply overhang.

H1 2026 interim results released: revenue RMB143.28bn (+1.2% YoY), gross profit RMB23.04bn (+25.1% YoY), gross margin 16.1% (up from 13.0%), overseas revenue ~RMB99bn (+51% YoY), NEV revenue +63.8% YoY to RMB59.28bn (41.4% of total revenue, up from 25.6%). Profit for the period RMB9.02bn (6.3% net margin, above China's ~3.8% auto-sector average); profit attributable to owners ~RMB8.57bn, reported down versus the prior-year comparative. Cash and equivalents RMB63.42bn (~US$9.4bn).

Q1 2026 results: revenue RMB65.87bn (down from RMB68.22bn in Q1 2025), gross profit improved to RMB10.56bn (16.0% margin) from RMB8.46bn (12.4% margin); profit attributable to owners RMB4.17bn, down from RMB4.65bn YoY, as R&D spend rose 25.5% and other expenses increased.

FY2025 annual results: record revenue RMB300.3bn (+11.3% YoY), net profit attributable to shareholders RMB19.5bn (+36.1% YoY), net margin 6.5%, record annual sales of 2.631 million units, 0.827 million NEVs sold, exports of 1.294 million vehicles (+33.2% YoY), becoming the first Chinese automaker to surpass 5 million cumulative exports. Europe sales +200% YoY; overseas NEV sales +500% YoY.

Chery completed its Hong Kong IPO, the largest global automotive IPO of 2025 and largest first-time HKEX IPO (excluding dual/secondary listings) since November 2022, raising ~HK$9.145bn (~US$1.2bn) at the top of its HK$30.75 price range; shares rose as much as ~11-14% on debut. Cornerstone investors included Hillhouse (HHLR), Greenwoods Asset Management, Dajia Life Insurance, Gotion Hong Kong, and state-owned entities.

guidance.as_of: H1 2026 Interim Report (August 20, 2026) and FY2025 Annual Report (March 2026) — Chery does not issue formal quantitative revenue/EPS guidance ranges in the manner typical of US-listed companies; forward-looking statements are qualitative strategic priorities rather than numeric targets

items.target: Five priorities for 2026: (i) expand product lineup/sharpen brand positioning, (ii) increase R&D investment in next-generation technologies, (iii) enhance vehicle electrification and intelligentization, (iv) expand international footprint via globalization strategy
items.vs_prior: maintained/reiterated from FY2025 annual report through H1 2026 interim report
items.notes: Company frames targets qualitatively around 'speed, scale, quality and profitability' rather than disclosing specific revenue, margin or unit-sales targets for FY2026.

items.vs_prior: reiterated (brand-level target, not formal company guidance)
items.notes: Cumulative Omoda/Jaecoo sales passed 1 million units (lifetime) as of April 2026; brand sales have reportedly doubled year-on-year for three consecutive years.

items.target: Solid-state batteries, large AI models, advanced smart/autonomous driving
items.notes: Named as 'cutting-edge core technologies' in the FY2025 chairman's statement prospects section; no capex or spending figures disclosed.

guidance.management_commentary: Chairman Yin Tongyue (FY2025 annual report, March 2026): framed 2025 as achieving 'five historic breakthroughs' (revenue, total sales, NEVs, exports, quality) and described 2026 industry competition as centering on 'electrification, intelligent technology, low-carbon solutions, AI, globalization, and premiumization.' H1 2026 interim MD&A reiterated that competition in both ICE and NEV markets 'remains intense' and that NEV demand 'may be cyclical, policy-driven, and volatile,' while highlighting overseas expansion (12 production bases including 3 overseas as of 30 June 2026) and plans to 'further expand product lineup and sharpen brand positioning' in H2 2026. No specific numeric revenue, margin or unit-sales guidance was provided for FY2026 or H2 2026 in the reviewed filings.

bull_case: Export leadership and overseas margin advantage: Chery is China's top vehicle exporter for 23 consecutive years, with overseas revenue growing 51% YoY in H1 2026 to ~RMB99bn and carrying higher margins than domestic sales, directly driving the group gross margin expansion from 13.0% to 16.1%

Rapid NEV mix shift with improving unit economics: NEV revenue share rose from 21.9% (2024) to 41.4% (H1 2026) while NEV gross margin improved from 0.4% to 8.8%+ over the same period, suggesting a long runway for margin convergence with ICE as scale builds

Diversified five-brand, multi-powertrain portfolio (CHERY/OMODA/JAECOO, JETOUR, EXEED, iCAR, LUXEED) spanning mass-market to premium/tech-forward segments, reducing single-model/single-brand concentration risk and supporting the strong momentum of Omoda/Jaecoo in Europe and the UK

Strong balance sheet and quality reputation: RMB63.4bn cash (~US$9.4bn) as of H1 2026, declining bank debt (RMB10.0bn vs. RMB23.2bn in FY2024), and #1 ranking among domestic brands across all five major J.D. Power quality studies support both financial flexibility and brand credibility for premiumization

Sell-side sentiment is uniformly bullish: multiple analysts (as of mid/late 2026) rate the stock a buy with price targets implying ~35-46% upside from various reference prices, reflecting confidence in the export/NEV growth story post-IPO
bear_case: Trade-policy risk is concentrated and worsening in Chery's most important growth markets: EU tariffs of 35.3% (plus 10% base duty) on Chinese EVs directly target the Europe growth engine (Omoda/Jaecoo), while 100%+ US tariffs and data-security rules keep the world's second-largest auto market closed indefinitely, with no confirmed entry timeline as of October 2026

Weak and uncertain domestic competitive position in NEVs: Chery holds only ~4.6% of China's domestic NEV retail market (7th place) versus BYD's ~23% and Geely's ~11%, meaning the bulk of Chery's NEV growth and margin improvement is leveraged to overseas markets that carry rising tariff and geopolitical risk

Margin and profit quality concerns beneath the headline growth: H1 2026 profit attributable to owners declined versus the prior-year period even as revenue and gross margin improved, driven by rising R&D spend, administrative costs, and a steep drop in other income/FX gains — and NEV gross margins, while improving, remain well below ICE margins, implying further mix-driven margin pressure as NEV share keeps rising

High leverage and working-capital strain: an 81.7% gearing ratio (up from 80.4%) and a 40.6% decline in net current assets in H1 2026, driven by inventory (+30.2%) and receivables (+19.5%) growing faster than cash, raise questions about the sustainability of export-driven growth funded increasingly through trade payables

Pre-IPO lock-up expiry overhang (reportedly ~US$8bn, as of September 2026) and Chery's short track record as a public company (listed only since September 2025) add near-term share-supply and governance-maturity uncertainty not yet tested through a full market cycle
